name: Guide arm: 4 Hz bilateral sine (Gateway Focus 10/12)
origin: This app's Gateway-style guides (our design; no published protocol)
summary: The coil arm of this project's Gateway-style Focus 10 and Focus 12 guides: the same 4 Hz sine on all temporal coils, in phase, at 2 uT for up to 32 min. It is this project's own design and untested. The Gateway documents describe sound through stereo headphones only; 4 Hz is their audio beat rate, not a field frequency from any source.
source: Our design after the Gateway research notes; Lane et al. 1998, Physiol Behav 63:249 (4 Hz binaural layer); Shakti safety page https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/safety.htm
notes: The Gateway method is sound through stereo headphones (McDonnell 1983 p.8; trip report 1982 p.1). None of the Gateway or Monroe documents this project holds describes magnetic or electrical stimulation. The 4 Hz is an audio beat frequency: the 1982 trip report speaks of 'internal four hertz heterodyning' (p.1), and Lane 1998 used binaural beats in 'the theta/delta range (1.5 and 4 Hz)' (p.1). This program plays a 4 Hz sine on all temporal coils in phase. Carrying an audio beat rate over to a magnetic field is this project's choice and has no source behind it. The guide's arm steps take 22 min. The program runs 32 min so that a paused guide does not cut it short (the helmet keeps running while the guide is paused), and the guide stops it after its last arm step. No source states a field strength, because none used a field; the 2 uT is this project's choice. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Nobody has tested this arm. The only cited statement on combining a coil device with binaural beats is a vendor's advice against it (Shakti safety page, rule 2: 'Do not combine Shakti with other mind machines in real-time.'). The arm exists only to test that combination under blinding: run it real against sham from the guide.
